questions.question: Q1. What is the default baseline vehicle speed value when the simulation environment initializes?

explanations.a: This is the minimum limit bound to the speed range slider input.
explanations.b: The default speed is set higher to reflect regional driving benchmarks.
explanations.c: The application code sets the default starting vehicle velocity slider directly to 70 km/h.
explanations.d: This represents the maximum operational speed value on the slider component.

questions.question: Q2. Which parameter tracks the total instantaneous energy of the moving vehicle on the Telemetry Panel?

explanations.a: This tracks the cumulative energy successfully captured back to the pack over time.
explanations.b: This measures the percentage gain relative to total battery capacity.
explanations.c: Initial Kinetic Energy computes and displays the real-time energy profile based on the current velocity.
explanations.d: This field displays qualitative diagnostic terms such as Stable or Traction Loss.

questions.question: Q3. What is the maximum regenerative force threshold that the simulated Motor-Generator Unit (MGU) can harvest?

explanations.a: This is the minimum boundary for the user brake force slider input.
explanations.b: The simulation code sets the MOTOR_REGEN_LIMIT constant to 1200 N; any force above this uses friction blending.
explanations.c: 1500 kg represents the baseline mass constant of the electric vehicle.
explanations.d: This is the maximum force scale factor bound to the control inputs.

questions.question: Q4. What visual indicator updates on the 2D canvas workspace when the vehicle enters an active wheel slip state?

answers.b: The grid lines stop moving entirely.
answers.c: The tire outer rings display red contour paths accompanied by a warning text overlay.
answers.d: The background canvas changes into a yellow diagnostic warning field.

explanations.a: Green indicates proper regenerative charging pulses, not structural traction loss.
explanations.b: Grid lines move relative to velocity until the vehicle comes to a absolute physical stop.
explanations.c: The drawing code turns the tire strokes red and prints a warning message when traction limits are violated.
explanations.d: The background grid retains its styling parameters throughout all operational execution states.

questions.question: Q5. What happens when you shift the Terrain Surface Grip configuration from Dry to Slippery Ice?

answers.b: The maximum road grip limit drops to its lowest value, inducing immediate wheel slip at low brake forces.
answers.c: The car instantly gains speed automatically.
answers.d: Regenerative braking efficiency automatically doubles to compensate.

explanations.a: Ice reduces the friction coefficient down to an experimental value of 0.10.
explanations.b: Slippery Ice restricts the available traction force, causing standard braking pressures to easily exceed road limits.
explanations.c: Velocity changes depend on the summation of applied brake force and grade incline profiles.
explanations.d: Efficiency drops due to the strict slip penalization algorithm triggered during traction loss.

questions.question: Q6. What baseline battery pack capacity value is utilized to calculate the State of Charge percentage gain?

explanations.a: The script hardcodes the battery capacity constant to 216,000,000 Joules to evaluate fractional charging returns.
explanations.b: This capacity represents a larger pack scale not utilized within this lab framework.
explanations.c: 1500 represents the mass constant configured for the translational model metrics.
explanations.d: 1200 represents the maximum force limit allocation configured for the MGU module.

questions.question: Q7. What warning layout configuration appears if the downhill gravity component completely overcomes the driver brake force?

answers.b: A red indicator accent box displays a 'Simulation Aborted: Vehicle cannot stop' notice.
answers.c: The charging particles turn bright purple.
answers.d: The telemetry logging stack clears its operational memory.

explanations.a: The workspace remains interactive to allow students to correct the unstable parameter inputs.
explanations.b: If the deceleration rate calculation drops to or below zero, a custom warning box renders over the canvas workspace.
explanations.c: Charging particles completely disengage since no forward deceleration torque is available for capture.
explanations.d: Telemetry outputs freeze at zero boundaries instead of wiping historic memory registers.

questions.question: Q8. What base efficiency value does the calculator start with prior to applying slope adjustments or slip penalties?

explanations.a: 45% represents the deduction penalty applied if the vehicle undergoes active wheel slip.
explanations.b: 65% is the final scaling factor applied under heavy traffic congestion environments.
explanations.c: The simulation source code initializes the calculation loop with a BASE_REGEN_EFFICIENCY constant of 0.82.
explanations.d: Ideal 100% efficiency is physically impossible due to electrical conversion and friction limitations.

questions.question: Q9. How large of an efficiency reduction penalty is applied if the tires lose traction grip during deceleration?

answers.c: The efficiency drops completely to 0% immediately.
answers.d: The penalty scales lineally with the slope angle profile.

explanations.a: A 10% shift does not sufficiently account for the severe kinetic losses of sliding friction profiles.
explanations.b: The calculator subtracts exactly 0.45 from the efficiency index whenever the wheel slip flag evaluates to true.
explanations.c: Some energy is still captured depending on the traffic density multiplier and grade baseline returns.
explanations.d: Slope variations adjust efficiency by a separate factor of -0.008 per degree index.

questions.question: Q10. What condition must be met for the Phase 2 navigation button to change from disabled to active?

answers.a: The reset parameters button must be pressed three times.
answers.b: The user must adjust the brake force slider beyond the minor deadband tolerance (>150 N) to run the simulation.
answers.c: The vehicle must come to a complete stop on an ice surface layer.
answers.d: The traffic condition dropdown must be set to heavy congestion mode.

explanations.a: Resetting parameters defaults workspace variables and locks Phase 2 access controls.
explanations.b: Applying brakes past the 150 N threshold toggles the operational flag that enables the Phase 2 mathematical verification sheets.
explanations.c: Traction loss statuses do not govern navigation unlocking routines within the interface script logic.
explanations.d: Traffic configurations alter local scalars but do not control core workspace sequence flags.
